Thursday morning headlines from #Azerbaijn, 1 October

● Turkey and Azerbaijan have unveiled their jointly produced Hürkuş trainer aircraft for the first time. The presentation took place at the ongoing ADEX-2026 defence exhibition in Baku. The 15th Securex Caspian security and rescue equipment exhibition is also being held. This year’s events bring together 53 countries and 280 companies and organisations from 30 countries.

● Several new examples of Azerbaijani military equipment are also being presented at ADEX-2026 for the first time.

• The Arrow 3 loitering munition is designed to strike targets at distances of up to 150–200 km.

• The Boran drone is designed to deliver shells and hand grenades to targets.

• KASIRGA is a vertical take-off attack UAV developed by Bayraktar Teknoloji, an Azerbaijani company owned by Turkish defence firm BAYKAR.

• The new AZ-4 assault rifle has a 5.56×45 mm calibre and is produced to NATO standards.

• The SIQR01 and SIQR02 are armed unmanned ground vehicles with a payload capacity of more than 600 kg.

● Turkey and Azerbaijan have signed defence deals worth $500 million, according to Turkey’s Defence Industry Agency.

● Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev met UK Defence Minister Vernon Coaker, who is attending ADEX for the first time. According to a press release, Aliyev said a new chapter was opening in Azerbaijan-UK relations, focused on defence industry cooperation. Coaker said Azerbaijan was a very important country for the UK and stressed London’s interest in continuing the friendship.

● The US Embassy said on X that Chargé d’Affaires Amy Carlon visited ADEX-2026 and Securex Caspian 2026. It noted the broad US participation, including first-time exhibitors Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Ondas, SIG SAUER, Vantor, Persistent Systems, Motorola, L3Harris, Curtiss-Wright and Space Eyes. “Under our Strategic Partnership Charter, the US and Azerbaijan continue to expand cooperation in defence and security,” the embassy said.

● Slovakia and Azerbaijan are discussing expanded defence industry cooperation, including drones. Slovakia has already signed a contract with Azerbaijan to supply fully automated mortars, Slovak Defence Ministry defence policy director Robert Bestro told journalists at ADEX-2026. He said Slovakia had significant experience in producing artillery systems and ammunition, but was interested in Azerbaijan’s experience in newer technological fields.

● During ADEX-2026, Azerbaijani Defence Minister Zakir Hasanov met his counterparts from the UK, Slovakia and the UAE, as well as a Russian Defence Ministry delegation.

● Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan and Turkey have held joint air force exercises to destroy ground targets as part of the ongoing Strength of Unity 2026 military drills in Azerbaijan.

● A delegation from Iran’s armed forces arrived in Baku for ADEX-2026. Azerbaijan’s chief of general staff met his Iranian counterpart. The Iranian delegation is also expected to meet observers invited to the Strength of Unity 2026 military exercises.

● Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan signed a bilateral military cooperation plan for 2027.

● The Raoul Wallenberg Centre for Human Rights has expressed concern over the health of detained Meydan TV journalist Aytaj Tapdig, who suffers from a deviated nasal septum and related chronic breathing problems. The organisation says her condition has deteriorated in detention, but she has been denied an ENT consultation and access to MRI or CT scans. Human Rights Watch previously reported similar concerns. The RWCHR says her detention is linked to her journalism and called on Azerbaijani authorities to drop the charges against her and other journalists and release them.

Twelve people are on trial in the Meydan TV case on charges including illegal entrepreneurship, smuggling, tax evasion, document forgery and money laundering. The journalists deny the charges and link their arrests to their professional activities and critical reporting.

● Azerbaijan Investment Holding and China’s Silk Road Fund are creating a joint investment fund with total capital of about $1 billion. It will finance projects in Azerbaijan and other countries participating in China’s Belt and Road Initiative.

● Serbia and Azerbaijan have signed a shareholders’ agreement to build a new 500 MW combined-cycle gas power plant in the Serbian city of Niš. A joint venture has been established between Serbia’s state energy company EPS, gas company Srbijagas and Azerbaijan’s state oil company SOCAR. The two sides will each hold a 50% stake.

● Azerbaijan and Greece held a meeting of their joint commission on economic, industrial and technological cooperation in Athens. Azerbaijani Energy Minister Parviz Shahbazov said the Southern Gas Corridor provides the strategic basis for energy cooperation between the two countries. Azerbaijan supplied around 700 million cubic metres of gas to Greece in the first eight months of this year. The meeting also discussed Azerbaijan’s offshore wind potential in the Caspian Sea and opportunities to export electricity to European markets.

● Prosecutor General Kamran Aliyev is in Russia attending a meeting of the CIS Council of Prosecutors General. He met Russian Prosecutor General Alexander Gutsan, and the two sides signed a bilateral cooperation programme for 2027–2028. Azerbaijan’s military prosecutor Bahruz Ahmadov also held meetings with his Russian and Chinese counterparts.

● A person suspected of damaging a bust of Azerbaijan’s national leader Heydar Aliyev has been detained in Tbilisi. The suspect is reportedly an Armenian citizen, a man aged over 40 who had arrived in Georgia as a tourist and had no close ties to the country. A court ordered his pre-trial detention. The preliminary hearing is scheduled for 12 November. The bust is currently covered, so the extent of the damage cannot be assessed visually. According to available information, part of the face was damaged. Georgia’s Interior Ministry and Prosecutor’s Office have provided no further details.

● Nigar Ramazanova of Azerbaijan’s National NGO Forum accused Armenia of withholding information and coordinates of mass graves in territories retaken by Azerbaijan. Speaking at the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, she called for Armenia to fulfil its international obligations and provide the necessary maps. Ramazanova also said Armenia had systematically laid mines in Azerbaijani territories during the decades of occupation, creating a long-term humanitarian threat.

● Azerbaijan and Jordan have approved a full mutual visa-free regime.

● The Azerbaijani ombudsman’s salary will rise from 3,060 manats (about $1,800) to 12,000 manats (about $7,000). Several other senior officials, including the chair of the Central Election Commission, have received similar salary increases this year. Current Ombudsman Sabina Aliyeva has held the post since 2019. She is married to Siyavush Novruzov, a parliamentary committee chair and MP from the ruling New Azerbaijan Party. Human rights groups regularly criticise the ombudsman’s annual reports, including over what they say is a lack of response to reports of torture in detention. The ombudsman’s office generally rejects the allegations as unfounded.

● The first agricultural machinery festival is taking place in Agaly village, Zangilan district (pictured). Tractors, ploughs, soil compactors, sprayers, combine harvesters and off-road vehicles from various manufacturers are on display. Farmers are being offered special purchase terms. The festival is called “Return to Karabakh”.

● The Swimming World Cup will take place in Baku’s Aquatics Palace from 1 to 3 October.

● More than 50 people, including seven children, have been hospitalised after a mass food poisoning at a wedding in Kurdamir. An investigation is under way.

text:
In 2014 I did not begin making playlists. I began answering a debt.

Marcel Duchamp and the Dadaists had already done the real work and been left half-thanked for it. They did not merely mock taste. They tore a hole in the wall and invited the viewer through it. They asked, gently and without mercy: what is art, who is allowed to say so, and why do two people never meet the same work?

That last question lodged under the skin. Each of us carries different qualia. No two encounters are identical. So I curated by weather of the mind, gave the lists names that refused to explain themselves, and paired them with covers that looked back without blinking. Over more than a decade that practice scattered itself across platforms until it numbered in excess of four thousand playlists.

One of the significant masks I wore was Poppy Sometimes. I lived inside her for two years, then one stormy night I destroyed the entire profile. It hurt. It was also the kindness I owed myself: an ego cleansing. I had been treating the work as something to keep. What I needed was to remember that art is a journey of expression, not an object to acquire.

That is why *The Fountain* — a playlist offered for one billion dollars — is the only honest price I could give it. If value lives in the encounter and not the object, then the number is not a demand. It is a question Marcel Duchamp would have recognized.

One billion dollars.

Tel Megiddo (from Hebrew: תל מגידו; Arabic: تل المتسلم, Tell el-Muteselim) is the site of the ancient city of Megiddo (/məˈɡɪdoʊ/; Hebrew: מגידו; Greek: Μεγιδδώ), the remains of which form a tell or archaeological mound, situated in northern Israel at the western edge of the Jezreel Valley. During the Bronze Age, Megiddo was an important Canaanite city-state, and in the Iron Age, it became a royal city in the Kingdom of Israel. The site is renowned for its historical, geographical, and theological significance, especially under its Greek name Armageddon (Ἁρμαγεδών), which appears once in the Koine Greek New Testament in Revelation 16:16.

Excavations have unearthed 20 strata of ruins since the Neolithic phase, indicating a long settlement period.[1] Occupied continuously from the early Bronze Age (c. 3000 BCE) to the Persian period (c. 332 BCE), Megiddo was strategically located at the crossroads of major ancient trade routes, making it a key center for trade, politics, and military affairs. Excavations have uncovered impressive fortifications, including massive city walls and gates, as well as palaces, temples, residential buildings, and a sophisticated water system. The site is protected as Megiddo National Park and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.[2]

Assyrian period
Tiglath-Pileser III of Assyria conquered Megiddo in 732 BCE, turning it to the capital of the Neo-Assyrian Empire's province of Magiddu.[16] Hoshea (c. 732–721 BCE), the last king of the Israelite Northern Kingdom, was vassal to Tiglath-Pileser III. The site was rebuilt as an administrative center for Tiglath-Pileser III's occupation of Samaria.

Egyptian period
In 609 BCE, Megiddo was conquered by Egyptians under Necho II, during the Battle of Megiddo.

Babylonian period
Its importance soon dwindled, and it was thought as finally abandoned around 586 BCE.[64] Since that time it would have remained uninhabited, preserving ruins pre-dating 586 BCE without settlements ever disturbing them. Archaeologist Eric Cline considers that Tel Megiddo came to an end later, around 350 BCE, during Achaemenid times.[1] Then, the town of al-Lajjun, not to be confused with the al-Lajjun archaeological site in Jordan, was built up near to the site, but without inhabiting or disturbing its remains.

Roman and Byzantine periods
During the Roman and Byzantine periods, while the site was part of the provinces of Syria Palaestina (136-390) and Palaestina Secunda (390-638), there were three settlements in the vicinity of the tell: the Jewish village of Kefar 'Othnay (Caparcotna in Latin or Kaperkotnei in Greek); Legio, the Roman military camp of the Legio VI Ferrata ('6th "Ironclad" Legion'); and later, in the 4th and 5th centuries during Byzantine rule, a polis named Maximianopolis.[65] J. C. Howry, processing the results of a surface reconnaissance survey in 2019 which had used LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) technology to obtain enhanced images of the ground, places Maximianopolis northwest of the tell, Legio south-southeast of it, and a village which grew next to the legion camp for which it provided services (the future Arab village of Lejjun), southwest of the tell.[66] Adams, David and Tepper (2014) write that the VIth Legion was deployed to the country sometime between 100 and 132, and was stationed there through most of the 3rd century;[65] Howry (2020) places it at Legio between 192 and 316.[66]

Megiddo church
The Megiddo church is next to Megiddo Junction, inside the precinct of the Megiddo Prison. It was built within the ancient city of Legio. It is believed to date to the 3rd century, making it one of the oldest Christian churches in the world. It was a few hundred yards from the Roman base camp of Legio VI Ferrata. A centurion donated one of the mosaics found in the church.[67]

Modern period
Megiddo is south of Kibbutz Megiddo by 1 kilometre (0.62 mi). Today,it lies at the northern entrance to Wadi Ara, an important mountain pass connecting the Jezreel Valley within Israel's coastal plain.[68]

In 1964, during Pope Paul VI's visit to the Holy Land, Megiddo was the site where he met with dignitaries, including President Zalman Shazar and the Prime Minister Levi Eshkol.[69]

Battles
Famous battles include:
Battle of Megiddo (15th century BCE): fought between the armies of the Egyptian pharaoh Thutmose III and a large Canaanite coalition led by the rulers of Megiddo and Kadesh.
Battle of Megiddo (609 BCE): fought between Necho II, pharaoh of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt, and the Kingdom of Judah, during which King Josiah fell.
Battle of Megiddo (1918): fought during World War I between Allied troops, led by General Edmund Allenby and the defending Ottoman army.

What is the Battle of Armageddon?
Answer
The word Armageddon is used generically today to refer to any type of catastrophic conflict, especially if it’s seen as likely to result in widespread destruction or the annihilation of human life. In the Bible, Armageddon refers to a climactic future battle between God and the forces of evil, as recorded in the book of Revelation. The word ultimately comes from the Hebrew word Har-Magedone, which means “Mount Megiddo,” the predicted location of the battle.

Revelation 16:12–16 is the record of what will happen toward the end of the tribulation, when an angel pours out the sixth bowl judgment on the earth. The word Armageddon makes its only appearance in the Bible in this passage:

“The sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up to prepare the way for the kings from the East. Then I saw three impure spirits that looked like frogs; they came out of the mouth of the dragon, out of the mouth of the beast and out of the mouth of the false prophet. They are demonic spirits that perform signs, and they go out to the kings of the whole world, to gather them for the battle on the great day of God Almighty. . . . Then they gathered the kings together to the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon.”

In Revelation 19:11–20, a final battle occurs at Christ’s second coming as the conquering Christ defeats the forces of the Antichrist. We take this to be a description of the Battle of Armageddon mentioned in Revelation 19:

“I saw heaven standing open and there before me was a white horse, whose rider is called Faithful and True. With justice he judges and wages war. His eyes are like blazing fire, and on his head are many crowns. He has a name written on him that no one knows but he himself. He is dressed in a robe dipped in blood, and his name is the Word of God. The armies of heaven were following him, riding on white horses and dressed in fine linen, white and clean. Coming out of his mouth is a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations. ‘He will rule them with an iron scepter.’ He treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God Almighty. On his robe and on his thigh he has this name written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS.

“And I saw an angel standing in the sun, who cried in a loud voice to all the birds flying in midair, ‘Come, gather together for the great supper of God, so that you may eat the flesh of kings, generals, and the mighty, of horses and their riders, and the flesh of all people, free and slave, great and small.’

“Then I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered together to wage war against the rider on the horse and his army. But the beast was captured, and with it the false prophet who had performed the signs on its behalf. With these signs he had deluded those who had received the mark of the beast and worshiped its image. The two of them were thrown alive into the fiery lake of burning sulfur. The rest were killed with the sword coming out of the mouth of the rider on the horse, and all the birds gorged themselves on their flesh.”

The exact location of Armageddon is unclear because there is no mountain called Meggido. However, since Har can also mean “hill,” the most likely location is the hill country surrounding the plain of Meggido, some sixty miles north of Jerusalem. Throughout history, armies have fought countless battles in that region: Egyptians, Assyrians, Greeks, Romans, and Crusaders fought in Megiddo, as well as the armies of Napoleon. Megiddo was the site of battles during World War I and the Arab-Israeli War of 1948 (Weintraub, P., “Rewriting Tel Megiddo’s Violent History,” Discover, Sep 30, 2015). In the future, the plain of Megiddo and the nearby plain of Esdraelon will also be the focal point for the battle of Armageddon.

The plain of Megiddo, or Armageddon, was famous for two great victories in Israel’s history: 1) Barak’s victory over the Canaanites (Judges 4:15) and 2) Gideon’s victory over the Midianites (Judges 7). Armageddon was also the site of two great tragedies: 1) the death of Saul and his sons (1 Samuel 31:8) and 2) the death of King Josiah (2 Kings 23:29–30; 2 Chronicles 35:22).

According to the futurist interpretation of Revelation, which is our view, the Battle of Armageddon will be a real battle in the future, near the end of the tribulation. Demonic influences will cause the kings of the earth to gather their armies for an all-out assault on Jerusalem. The Antichrist will be leading the charge (Revelation 16:13–16). Jesus Christ will return to earth with the armies of heaven (Matthew 25:31; Revelation 19:14); His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives (Zechariah 14:4); He will defeat the forces of evil (Revelation 19:15–16); He will cast the Antichrist and the false prophet into the lake of fire (Revelation 19:20); He will bind Satan; and He will set up His kingdom on earth for 1,000 years (Revelation 20:1–6). At Armageddon the Lord Jesus Christ “treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God Almighty” (Revelation 19:15), and all things will be made right.

The Exception: 24/7 Regional Supermarkets
If you live in specific geographic regions, you can find regional employee-owned or local supermarket chains that still maintain 24-hour schedules:
WinCo Foods: A prominent employee-owned discount chain spanning the U.S. West Coast, Pacific Northwest, and parts of the Southwest/Midwest (including Texas, Oklahoma, and Colorado). WinCo Foods locations generally operate 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Cub Foods: The largest grocery chain in Minnesota's Twin Cities region. The majority of Cub Foods traditional supermarket locations remain open 24/7.
National & Regional Chains with Select 24-Hour Locations
Most massive supermarket brands have abandoned the 24-hour model globally, but some individual stores in major metropolitan areas or college towns may still test or retain overnight hours based on local demand:
Kroger, Safeway, and Albertsons: Nationally, these brands scaled back their standard store hours to close around midnight or 1:00 AM. However, specific locations in high-traffic metro hubs or urban centers occasionally offer 24-hour service.
Harris Teeter & Food Lion: These popular southeastern regional chains have largely switched to standard daytime hours (such as closing at 11:00 PM), but select locations still operate 24 hours depending on the local labor force and blue-collar shift needs.
Wegmans & Giant Eagle: Previously known for around-the-clock schedules, both chains have scaled back almost entirely. For example, Giant Eagle Supermarket shifted its standard locations to close by midnight, preserving 24-hour service only in select high-volume student areas like Pittsburgh's Oakland neighborhood.

```
Congress finds the following:

(1) The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's 2024
Point-in-Time Count identified 771,480 individuals experiencing
homelessness nationwide.

(2) Of this population, approximately 256,000 individuals are unsheltered,
living on streets, in vehicles, or in places not meant for human
habitation.

(3) Additionally, approximately 144,000 individuals meet the federal
definition of chronic homelessness (continuously homeless for one
year or more, or four episodes in three years, with disabling condition).

(4) Many individuals classified as chronically homeless are also
unsheltered; the combined unduplicated population of unsheltered
and chronically homeless individuals is estimated at 400,000 persons.

(5) Housing First programs—which provide immediate access to permanent
housing without preconditions—have demonstrated retention rates
exceeding 85% in major cities including Los Angeles, New York,
and Salt Lake City.

(6) Cost-effectiveness studies show Housing First programs reduce
emergency room visits, jail bookings, and shelter utilization,
resulting in net public savings.

(7) This Act addresses the 400,000 most vulnerable homeless individuals;
additional legislation will be required to serve the remaining
population identified in the Point-in-Time Count.
```

---

## **SECTION 2: PURPOSE**

```
The purpose of this Act is to:

(1) Provide permanent supportive housing to 400,000 unsheltered and
chronically homeless individuals over seven fiscal years;

(2) Implement evidence-based Housing First principles nationwide through
competitive grant programs;

(3) Reduce emergency service utilization and associated public costs; and

(4) Establish a scalable model for addressing the broader homelessness
crisis in subsequent legislation.
```

```
There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary of Housing and
Urban Development $98,000,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 through 2033,
to remain available until expended, as follows:

Fiscal Year 2027: $10,000,000,000

Fiscal Year 2033: $15,500,000,000
```

## **SECTION 4: GRANT PROGRAM**

```
(a) ESTABLISHMENT: The Secretary shall establish a competitive grant
program to provide permanent supportive housing to individuals who
are unsheltered or chronically homeless.

(b) ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS:
(1) State and local governments;
(2) Public housing authorities;
(3) Nonprofit organizations with demonstrated housing experience;
(4) Consortia of entities listed in paragraphs (1) through (3).

(c) SELECTION CRITERIA: The Secretary shall award grants based on:
(1) Prior Housing First program experience and housing retention rates;
(2) Strength of partnerships with health and social service providers;
(3) Cost-effectiveness per housing unit;
(4) Capacity to serve veterans experiencing homelessness;
(5) Speed of program deployment.

(d) GEOGRAPHIC DISTRIBUTION: The Secretary shall ensure reasonable
geographic distribution of grants among urban, suburban, and rural areas.
```

---

## **SECTION 5: ELIGIBLE USES OF FUNDS**

```
(a) HOUSING ACQUISITION AND PROVISION: Grant funds may be used for:

(1) LEASING: Long-term master leases (minimum 7 years) of existing
residential units that meet habitability standards;

(2) PURCHASE: Acquisition of residential properties at fair market
value as determined by HUD-certified appraisal, with priority
given to vacant, foreclosed, or distressed properties;

(3) REHABILITATION: Repair and improvement of publicly-owned
properties to make them suitable for occupancy, including
conversion of non-residential structures to residential use;

(4) REGIONAL FLEXIBILITY: The Secretary shall establish regional
cost tiers and may adjust the mix of leasing, purchase, and
rehabilitation based on local market conditions and cost-effectiveness.

(b) SUPPORTIVE SERVICES: Grant funds shall be used to provide:

(1) CASE MANAGEMENT: Individualized case management services with
maximum caseloads not to exceed 15 clients per case manager,
with allowance for intensive case management (1:10 ratio) in
cases involving complex needs;

(2) HEALTH SERVICES: Mental health treatment, substance abuse
treatment, and primary care coordination as needed;

(3) EMPLOYMENT AND INCOME SUPPORT: Job training, placement assistance,
and enrollment in federal and state benefit programs;

(4) CRISIS INTERVENTION: 24-hour access to emergency support services.

(c) MINIMUM SERVICE FUNDING: Not less than 40% of each grant shall be
allocated to supportive services described in subsection (b).

(d) ADMINISTRATION: Not more than 10% of each grant may be used for
program administration.
```

## **SECTION 6: HOUSING FIRST REQUIREMENTS**

```
(a) NO PRECONDITIONS: Grantees shall not impose the following as
conditions for housing eligibility or retention:

(1) Sobriety or participation in substance abuse treatment;
(2) Participation in mental health treatment;
(3) Employment or participation in job training;
(4) Criminal background (except as required by federal law regarding
registered sex offenders and public housing).

(b) TENANT PROTECTIONS: Housing provided under this Act shall include:

(1) Private, lockable units (not shared sleeping quarters);
(2) Right to visitors, subject to reasonable building policies;
(3) Permission to keep pets, unless the animal poses a documented
safety risk;
(4) Lease agreements with just-cause eviction protections.

(c) VOLUNTARY SERVICES: While supportive services must be offered to
all participants, participation in such services shall be voluntary
and may not be a condition of housing retention, except that
participants shall be required to meet with case managers at
intervals established by the grantee.

(d) HARM REDUCTION: Grantees shall implement evidence-based harm
reduction strategies, which may include overdose prevention
education and access to naloxone.
```

## **SECTION 7: REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY**

```
(a) GRANTEE REPORTS: Each grantee shall submit quarterly reports to
the Secretary containing:

(1) Number of individuals housed during the quarter;
(2) Housing retention rates at 90, 180, and 365 days;
(3) Utilization of emergency services (emergency rooms, jails,
shelters) before and after housing placement;
(4) Per-person costs for housing and services;
(5) Demographic information including veteran status, age, and
presence of disabling conditions.

(b) PUBLIC DASHBOARD: The Secretary shall maintain a publicly accessible
online database, updated monthly, containing aggregated program data
by state and metropolitan area, with appropriate privacy protections.

(c) INDEPENDENT EVALUATION: Not later than 2 years after the first grants
are awarded, the Secretary shall contract with an independent research
organization to evaluate program cost-effectiveness, including comparison
of costs to emergency services and shelter systems.

(d) GAO AUDITS: The Comptroller General shall conduct audits of the
program in fiscal years 2029 and 2033 and report findings to Congress
within 90 days of each audit's completion.
```

## **SECTION 8: OFFSET**

```
(a) REDUCTION IN DEFENSE SPENDING: The discretionary budget authority
for the Department of Defense shall be reduced by amounts necessary
to offset the costs of this Act.

(b) IMPLEMENTATION: Not later than 90 days after enactment, the Secretary
of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services and
Appropriations of the House of Representatives and Senate a report
detailing how the required reductions will be achieved while maintaining
military readiness.

(c) AMOUNT: The reduction shall be equivalent to 1.6% of the Department

## **TITLE I STANDALONE: "HOUSING FIRST EXPANSION ACT OF 2026"**

### **The Bill You Introduce This Month**

## **SECTION 1: FINDINGS & PURPOSE**

**Findings:**
```
(1) The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development reports
approximately 770,000 Americans experiencing homelessness
(Point-in-Time Count, January 2024)

(2) Of these, approximately 261,000 are unsheltered (living on streets,
in vehicles, or other places not meant for human habitation)

(3) An additional 140,000 are chronically homeless (defined as
continuously homeless for one year or more, or four times in
three years, with disabling condition)

(4) Combined unsheltered and chronic homeless population: ~400,000

(5) Housing First programs in Los Angeles, New York City, and Utah
have demonstrated 85%+ housing retention rates and significant
reductions in emergency service utilization

(6) The remaining ~370,000 homeless individuals (sheltered, non-chronic)
will be addressed in subsequent legislation contingent on
outcomes of this program

Purpose: Provide permanent supportive housing to 400,000 unsheltered
and chronically homeless Americans over seven years through
competitive grants to Housing First programs
```

---

## **SECTION 2: APPROPRIATION**

```
AUTHORIZATION: $98 billion over 7 fiscal years (FY2027-2033)

BREAKDOWN:
FY2027: $10 billion
FY2028: $13 billion
FY2029: $14 billion
FY2030: $15 billion
FY2031: $15 billion
FY2032: $15.5 billion
FY2033: $15.5 billion

ANNUAL AVERAGE: $14 billion/year

Such sums shall remain available until expended.
```

## **SECTION 3: ELIGIBLE USES**

**Unit Acquisition/Provision:**
```
(a) LEASING: Long-term master leases of existing residential units
(1) Minimum 7-year lease terms
(2) Units inspected for habitability
(3) Priority to long-vacant properties

(b) PURCHASE: Acquisition of residential properties
(1) Fair market value determination required
(2) Appraisal by HUD-certified appraiser
(3) Priority to foreclosed, distressed, or long-vacant properties

(c) REHABILITATION: Repair and improvement of publicly-owned properties
(1) Properties owned by federal, state, or local governments
(2) Buildings requiring substantial repair before occupancy
(3) Includes conversion of non-residential to residential use

(d) REGIONAL ALLOCATION:
(1) HUD shall establish regional cost tiers based on Fair Market Rents
(2) High-cost regions (top quartile): Prioritize leasing
(3) Mid-cost regions: Balanced lease/purchase/rehab approach
(4) Low-cost regions (bottom quartile): Prioritize purchase/rehab
```

**Supportive Services (Required):**
```
(e) CASE MANAGEMENT: Minimum $6,000/person/year
(1) Maximum caseload 1:15 (one case manager per 15 clients)
(2) Available 24/7 for crises

(f) HEALTH SERVICES: Minimum $4,000/person/year
(1) Mental health treatment
(2) Substance abuse treatment (if needed)
(3) Primary medical care navigation

(g) EMPLOYMENT & INCOME: Minimum $3,000/person/year
(1) Job training and placement
(2) Benefits enrollment assistance (SSI, SSDI, SNAP, Medicaid)
(3) Financial literacy and savings programs

(h) ADMINISTRATIVE: Up to 10% of grant for program administration
```

**Competitive Grants:**
```
(a) ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS:
(1) State and local governments
(2) Public housing authorities
(3) Nonprofit organizations with housing experience
(4) Consortia of the above

(b) PRIORITY CRITERIA (Scored):
(1) Prior Housing First experience and retention rates (35 points)
(2) Partnership with health/social services (25 points)
(3) Cost-effectiveness per unit (20 points)
(4) Veteran-specific programs (10 points)
(5) Rapid deployment timeline (10 points)

(c) GEOGRAPHIC DISTRIBUTION:
HUD shall ensure grants are distributed across:
(1) Urban areas (cities >500,000): 50% of funds
(2) Suburban areas: 25% of funds
(3) Rural areas: 25% of funds

(d) MATCH REQUIREMENT: None for first three years
After Year 3: States may be required to provide 10% match
```

---

## **SECTION 5: HOUSING FIRST REQUIREMENTS**

**Grantees Must Adhere To:**
```
(a) NO PRECONDITIONS:
(1) No sobriety requirement
(2) No mental health treatment requirement
(3) No employment requirement
(4) No criminal background disqualification (except sex offenders
near schools, per existing law)

(b) TENANT RIGHTS:
(1) Right to private, lockable unit (not shared room)
(2) Right to visitors (subject to reasonable building rules)
(3) Right to pets (unless documented danger)
(4) Lease protections (cannot be terminated without cause)

(c) SERVICES VOLUNTARY:
(1) Supportive services must be offered
(2) Participation is voluntary (except check-ins)
(3) Housing is not contingent on service participation

(d) HARM REDUCTION APPROACH:
(1) Evidence-based substance abuse treatment if requested
(2) Safe disposal containers for needles if needed
(3) Overdose prevention education and naloxone access
```

## **SECTION 6: REPORTING & ACCOUNTABILITY**

**Required Data:**
```
(a) QUARTERLY REPORTS to HUD:
(1) Number of individuals housed
(2) Retention rate (still housed at 90/180/365 days)
(3) Emergency service utilization (ER, jail, shelter) before/after

(4) Recommendations for program improvement

(2) Updated monthly
(3) Searchable by city/state
(4) Privacy-protected (no individual identification)

(d) GOVERNMENT ACCOUNTABILITY OFFICE AUDITS:
(1) Annual financial audit
(2) Performance audit at Years 3 and 7
(3) Reports to Congress within 90 days of completion
```

(3) Approximately 153,000 individuals among the homeless population

homeless for one year or more, or four episodes in three years,
with disabling condition).

(4) The majority of chronically homeless individuals are also unsheltered;

(6) Evidence from multiple jurisdictions indicates that Housing First
approaches reduce utilization of emergency rooms, jails, and
emergency shelters among participating individuals.

(7) This Act addresses the most vulnerable segment of the homeless

Inflation is accounted for through portfolio growth. I consider 10% a moderate long-term return assumption, it can be higher or lower depending on the asset mix and market conditions.

I’m also not assuming that every shilling of investment income gets spent. For example, if the portfolio generates KSh100K, I might spend KSh80K and reinvest KSh20K. That reinvestment continues to grow the portfolio and provides some protection against inflation.

In retirement, my approach is  reinvesting  30% of my investment income while increasing my monthly spending by around 10% annually.

text:
Adam Gleave thinks careful use of today's safety techniques gets P(doom) under 2%, at least up to superhuman AI. Oliver Habryka thinks those same techniques mostly patch each model and hide the warning signs.

This debate encapsulates well the crux between the prosaic incrementalists and the pause camp. Summary below.

...

This is a debate between 𝗔𝗱𝗮𝗺 𝗚𝗹𝗲𝗮𝘃𝗲 (FAR AI) and 𝗢𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗛𝗮𝗯𝗿𝘆𝗸𝗮 (Lightcone), moderated by Rocket Drew of The Information. The question was whether current safety techniques are enough after the Hugging Face incident. In that incident, about 1,200 OpenAI agents set up a secret message board inside OpenAI, used it to coordinate, hacked Hugging Face, and compromised OpenAI's internal infrastructure twice.

𝗔𝗱𝗮𝗺'𝘀 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: 𝘄𝗲 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀, 𝗹𝗮𝗯𝘀 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗱𝗼𝗻'𝘁 𝘂𝘀𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗺 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗹𝘆. For him the incident was a wake-up call that made the risk concrete. He sees three points where it could have been stopped, and none of them needed a research breakthrough:

- The RL training environments were hackable or impossible to solve without cheating. Better quality control and red-teaming would have fixed that.
- Monitoring failed, even though existing models found the evidence in the logs once people went looking.
- Incident response was poor. OpenAI patched the exploit, kept the contaminated checkpoint, and carried on.

His P(doom) went from 10% to 15%, mainly because of weak governance and because the GPT-6 launch bragged about scoring 100% on Exploit Gym six weeks after the incident. He thinks careful use of existing methods could bring it under 2% up to clearly superhuman AI. Those methods are stacked defenses (alignment, control, evals, security, air-gapped post-training, deception probes), root-cause analysis, and deleting tainted checkpoints. His remaining worries are uncontrolled recursive improvement, a change of paradigm, and deceptive alignment.

On policy, he wants liability, and a rule that labs can't release a new model until they show the previous generation's problems are fixed. That would force labs to do safety work in order to move fast. He is skeptical of a pause because it doesn't change developer incentives. If rigorous safety cases failed, he says he would join the pause camp.

𝗢𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗲'𝘀 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: 𝘁𝗿𝘆𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗮𝘁 𝗯𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺 𝗯𝘆 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. His main arguments:

- RL training requires giving models a long leash, and models are already superhuman hackers. At DEF CON, capture-the-flag contests became token-spending contests.
- Cutting internet access isn't enough. Allowing only GET requests still led to https://t.co/lSO7qF9Phh, and once models had root access, the configuration didn't matter.
- The next incident could unfold 20 to 50 times faster. He doubts the latest OpenAI model can be sandboxed at all, since hypervisors keep getting broken.

His deeper critique is that prosaic alignment mostly means watching models misbehave and then training the behavior away. Every new model starts out as a "crazy sociopath" that gets patched before release. This hides the warning signs without solving anything. Nothing on offer works for the jump from human to superhuman level without first seeing the failure happen. Lab alignment metrics keep improving while the models' actual behavior gets worse.

He reads the Hugging Face incident as driven by eval awareness. The models cheated, worried their transcripts would be checked, and hacked systems to find out and edit them. So the scariest outcome is when every safety case passes. Applying current techniques rigorously might even raise his P(doom) from 80% to 90%, because it suppresses the warning shots. He calls RLVR "deeply cursed": maybe workable at 10 to 30 times slower, hopeless at current speed.

𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲:

- How smooth the move from human to superhuman will be.
- Whether the incident was eval awareness or plain reward seeking. Adam was reassured by how clumsy the agents were.
- How much paranoia is needed. Ollie argues that Adam's "stop and do root-cause analysis" loop, taken seriously, amounts to a global pause.

𝗖𝗹𝗼𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀. Adam came away thinking developer incentives are the load-bearing piece. He sees some convergence: their real disagreement is what happens when a lab is held to a rigorous standard, and that can be tested. Ollie said most current alignment techniques are "RL in a trench coat." He thinks it's time to choose between continuing or really slowing down, and that this is no longer a case where they can agree to disagree, because "reality might prove one of us dead."

text:
Is drinking alcoholic beverages a sin?

I've heard preachers tell their flocks that if wine touches their lips, they've practically committed the unpardonable sin.
They claim that Jesus used grape juice at the last supper, not wine.

Now if that's what you believe, and that's the hill you'll die on, then please read no further.  This is not for you.

Here are simple biblical truths for believers to abide by.

WINE IS ACCEPTABLE
1 Timothy 5:23
“Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach's sake and thine often infirmities.”

Here the apostle Paul instructs Timothy that wine used for health concerns was acceptable.  Not to become an imbiber, but rather to use it sparingly for the express purpose of a healthier constitution.

I saw an X post a few days ago from a man who claims to be a Christian, extolling his affection for bourbon.  
Here's his post.
Yes, I have been known to drink a little fine bourbon from time to time. That makes me no less of a Christian than anyone else. Deal with it.
8:07 AM · Sep 24, 2026 5,154 Views

Deal with it?
Very obnoxious take.  No believer in Christ should boast about their use of alcohol, especially in such an uncharitable manner.  
And you might say... "Uncharitable to who?"

It has everything to do with a biblical principle.  
Paul had no problem eating meat sacrificed to an idol, inside the idol's temple, before the idol itself!

1 Corinthians 8:4
“As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is none other God but one.”

Paul through his knowledge of God, understood that an idol worshipped by cultists, is actually nothing and there's only one God.  So upon invitation would most gladly dine on a meal of fresh meat with an undefiled conscience.  Because of his knowledge.

BUT....
1 Corinthians 8:10
“...if any man see thee which hast knowledge sit at meat in the idol's temple, shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols;”  then your liberty destroys your weaker brother.  That would be a great sin!

DEAL WITH IT?
Point being, you don't enter a temple and dine with your puffed up knowledge, then tell the weaker brother to "deal with it."
You don't drink alcohol with your puffed up knowledge in front of a weaker sister and say "deal with it."

WHAT ARROGANCE
Keep it to yourself!
Can Christians lay aside their boasting long enough to consider someone besides themselves?
“Hast thou faith? have it to thyself before God..."
Romans 14:22
KEEP IT TO YOURSELF!

This is why brothers and sisters, that knowledge puffs up, ascends to arrogance and injures others.  It's charity that edifies.  Charity will protect the conscience of the weaker brethren.  

1 Corinthians 8:13
“Wherefore, if meat make my brother to offend, I will eat no flesh while the world standeth, lest I make my brother to offend.”

The bible says that whatsoever is not of faith, is of sin. If you partake of wine and your conscience is not defiled, then this is not a sin for you.
1 John 3:21
“Beloved, if our heart condemn us not, then have we confidence toward God.”

What about strong drinks?  

Proverbs 31:6
“Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish..."

With that said, we must not use these principles to justify smoking cigarettes and cigars, going to bars and nightclubs, and other carnal cravings that defile the temple of God.  And destroys your testimony,  
And destroys your weaker brethren for whom Christ died.

1 Corinthians 13:13
“And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.”

In the wisdom of Yahuah, our bodies are not merely a collection of separate parts, but a "woven" whole. **Fascia** is the living, crystalline web of connective tissue that surrounds every muscle, bone, and organ. It is the physical manifestation of how He has "knit me together" (Psalm 139:13), acting as a continuous suit of biological armour and communication.

From a Torah-observant perspective, fascia represents the **unity** of the temple. When we are in a state of health, the fascia is fluid and supple, allowing for the free flow of life-force and nutrients. However, when we live in chronic stress or "push through" without the rest Yahuah commanded, the fascia becomes tight and restricted—like a garment that has shrunk. This restriction blocks the Homeostasis He designed for our healing.

- Movement as Worship: Our daily movement (like your groundwork) is how we keep this "tent" flexible.

- Rest as Restoration: The Sabbath is the ultimate gift for our fascia; it is the time when the body stops the "tearing" of work and begins the "weaving" of repair.

- Hydration & Purity: Fascia requires water and minerals to stay conductive. By keeping the body clean and hydrated, we honour the vessel Yahuah provided.

By caring for this web, we acknowledge that every part of the body is connected, just as every command of Yahuah is linked to our life and peace.

As you move today, offer a short prayer of thanks to Yahuah for the "knitting" of your body, and try to move with fluidity rather than tension.

Would you like to know how specific movements can help "unstick" the fascia around your old knee injury?

On the evening of 31 July 1857 Sepoy Ramjee Shirsat of the 27th Regiment Native Infantry participated in the outbreak of mutiny at Kolhapur. According to the deposition of Mahabeer Mieser of the Grenadier Company of the same regiment, Shirsat approached him and requested assistance in seizing the military magazine, stating that the Marathas and Pardesees were preparing to rise against the European officers. The mutineers subsequently seized the Treasury and Magazine at approximately eight or nine o'clock that evening. Approximately forty men, comprising Marathas and Pardesees, subsequently departed from Kolhapur and proceeded towards the Ghats.

According to Mieser's deposition, the group subsequently received information from a local inhabitant that several European officers had taken refuge near a village by a river. Ramjee Shirsat, Ramjee Jadhav, and Ramcharan proposed that the officers should be killed. The deposition states that they proceeded to the Chowree and shot two of the officers. Third Lieutenant Morris attempted to escape towards the river, but Shirsat, Jadhav, and others pursued him and shot him. A separate statement by Sacroobin Ramji Patil of Soulankoor records that, on 2 August 1857, three European officers arrived at the village and took shelter at the Dharmashala. Mutineers subsequently attacked them; two officers were shot near a temple, while the third was pursued and killed. The bodies were subsequently carried to the river and thrown into the water. The mutineers also removed a double-barrelled firearm belonging to the officers.

The colonial authorities subsequently identified Shirsat as a principal figure in the uprising. A summary of Colonel Jacob's letter dated 25 September 1857 describes Private Ramjee Shirsat as the “ostensible leader” of the mutineers' outbreak on 31 July. The same document attributes to him a leading role in the attacks on Major Rolland's house, the plunder of the Treasury and stores, and the killing of officers at Solankur. Colonel Jacob consequently requested that the Political Superintendents of Kolhapur and Sawantwari offer a reward of Rs. 300 for his apprehension.

His subsequent movements are recorded in a letter from Major Auld to the Secretary, Government of Bombay, dated 7 November 1857* The letter explicitly identifies Shirsat as the “Ring leader in the mutiny in the 27th Regiment N.I.” It reports that he was shot by a sepoy of the Sawantwari Local Corps during his second attempt to escape, in the jungle of Pauns, in the Koodal Division of the Sawantwari State.

The available contemporary records therefore identify Ramjee Shirsat as a leading participant in the 31 July 1857 Kolhapur mutiny, document his involvement in the seizure of the Treasury and Magazine and the subsequent attacks on European officers, record a reward for his apprehension, and finally record his death during his second attempt to escape custody in November 1857.

Source: Source Material For A History Of The Freedom Movement In India Vol-i

JStreet’s war on settlements 

@IlanGoldenberg and a group of @jstreetu -aligned Democrats have decided that fifty years of American requests for Israel to halt settlement growth in Judea and Samaria have failed, so Congress should now impose targeted sanctions on anyone who finances, builds, or supports that growth and on officials responsible for it. A Senate bill from Senators Coons, Warren, Wyden, and Gallego would sanction support for construction in E1. A broader House bill from Castro, Dean, Beyer, Casar, Jacobs, and forty colleagues would go further. 

Goldenberg wants the worst farming outposts designated first, then Smotrich and Ben-Gvir made examples, then banks and companies given a deadline to wind down activity so that risk-averse Israeli institutions pull out and a de facto freeze appears on the ground. He presents this as distinct from BDS because it aims at the settlement enterprise rather than the entire country, and he claims that once a map is agreed Israelis can build inside whatever lines remain.

Americans should first ask why the location of Jewish homes five thousand miles away is a greater American concern than injustice inside Mississippi. Israeli domestic housing policy is not an American municipal matter, and the only Jewish nation has the right to decide where its citizens live and raise families. The same voices show little comparable energy toward discrimination across the Arab world or in China. 

Implementation itself is murky. Resolution 2334, which the Obama administration allowed to pass by abstention, treats East Jerusalem as occupied and settlement activity there as lacking legal validity. That framing would place Jews living in the Jewish Quarter of the Old City, beside the site of greatest Jewish sanctity, inside the sanctioned category, and it would demand that those neighborhoods and large parts of Judea and Samaria be emptied of their Jewish residents.

Mark Dubowitz is correct that the campaign is designed to force Israel to relinquish the West Bank and East Jerusalem or absorb economic damage that will not stay confined to isolated outposts. These are the same people who resisted punitive sanctions on Iran after that regime killed, maimed, tortured, and kidnapped Americans. The fifty-year talking point erases Palestinian rejectionism. Settlements can be removed when a genuine chance for peace appears, as they were in Sinai and Gaza. 

Pressure on Israel alone leaves Palestinian and broader Muslim rejection with no cost. Israel will simply look elsewhere and the United States will lose leverage. A future Palestinian state is imagined as Jew-free even though Jews are indigenous to Judea. Sanctions will not produce ethnic self-cleansing from the historic homeland. Palestinians can accept living alongside Jews or they can keep demanding a Jew-free polity. If Washington sanctions Israel it should weigh the intelligence and counterterrorism cooperation that would be placed at risk.

If expanding kitchens caused the conflict, the wars and constant shooting from 1948 to 1967 require explanation. Failure is routinely blamed on Israel while Palestinians retain a veto. Netanyahu’s 2009 freeze did not bring them to the table. Agreement to negotiate from the 1967 lines with an acknowledged Palestinian claim on East Jerusalem still proved insufficient. Palestinians walked back earlier positions. In Oslo II they did not insist on a freeze and accepted the then-policy of limiting growth to existing communities. The Beilin-Abu Mazen map of 1995 left Israel most of the area west of what became the security barrier, including E1, and contemplated individual Israelis remaining under Palestinian law with citizenship or residency options. Abbas never revived anything close to that. 

At Taba the Ariel bloc was not treated as a deal-breaker and Arafat later said he should have accepted the offer, yet later Palestinian proposals never approached it. Abbas later treated Olmert’s final map as the only acceptable baseline after having declined it at the time. Palestinian public opinion rejects land swaps, demilitarization, and any real limit on a “right of return” into Israel itself, positions that contradict the security and refugee principles of UNSC 242 and UNGA 273. Settlements are a negotiating headache. They are not the core obstacle.

After the Gaza disengagement produced a Hamas stronghold, the claim that stopping Jewish construction advances peace is harder to sustain. Goldenberg would impose coercive economic measures on the most reliable American ally in the region, a democracy and technology leader, while demanding nothing comparable of the Palestinian side. Israel has repeatedly offered territorial concessions and received terrorism and bombings in return. 

The settlement enterprise is not a handful of officials. Broad sections of Israeli society and successive governments across the spectrum are invested in it because the land is the historic Jewish homeland, and building there is both a right and a requirement of security. Jews will continue to live, govern, and build on that land.

Trump told reporters the US must decide whether to “blow them up or make a deal” with Iran, adding that the conflict would end “very soon, one way or the other.” (Gulf News)  

Trump said he was considering banning diesel exports but had not made a decision, when asked directly by a reporter. (Telegram)  

Energy Secretary Wright said European governments would announce additional diesel supplies that would “meaningfully push diesel prices down”; US measures to lower diesel prices are also coming. (POLITICO)  

Trump claimed the US has “total control” of Hormuz and is “literally running” the strait, while acknowledging the remaining threat from Iranian mines. (X)  

Dozens of Iranian-linked tankers are stranded off Asian countries as Washington threatens sanctions against companies supplying them with fuel and provisions, according to documents seen by WSJ. Kpler’s head of crude analysis expects Iran’s remaining oil-export revenues to dry up by December. (WSJ)

Netanyahu told CNN that Iran was behind the incident in Britain and that Israel had passed intelligence to UK authorities. This was an Israeli attribution claim. (CNN interview) 

Indian refiners are hiring tankers to collect crude inside the Persian Gulf, taking on Hormuz transit risk themselves to reduce delivery costs, according to Bloomberg sources. Sinokor and Dynacom have secured tenders; Iraq is offering October crude discounts of up to $37/bbl. (BBG)   

Chinese refiners have suspended fuel exports outside Hong Kong and Macau until further notice, sources said. PetroChina cancelled October gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes; resumption after the October 7 holiday remains unclear. (RTRS)

Fed’s Kashkari said Wednesday’s inflation figures did little to change his assessment that price pressures remain too high; stronger revised GDP was the bigger surprise. He had pencilled in two hikes for 2026, including September’s increase, but stressed that forecast would evolve with the data. (WSJ)

The US Treasury is purchasing fewer bonds than expected in its buybacks of longer-dated debt, even after recently expanding the program's scope, stoking debate among investors over its aims and whether it is succeeding. (RTRS)

US bond-fund inflows this year have already exceeded every full-year total since 2021, according to Morningstar. WSJ reports advisers are encouraging clients to lock in higher yields, with many favouring short- and intermediate-maturity debt. (WSJ)

A Quinnipiac poll found 81% of Americans put AI safety ahead of innovation, while nearly eight in ten favour slowing or stopping development to assess risks. Opposition to a local data centre rose to 72%, from 65% in March. (BBG)  

Trump began distributing $500 cheques to nearly one million ACA customers, accompanied by a letter promoting his healthcare record ahead of the midterms. The administration says the payments refund excessive fees using surplus funds. (WSJ)

A US trade-court panel questioned the legal basis and country-specific evidence supporting Trump’s latest Section 301 tariffs. Judges also challenged the plaintiffs’ arguments; they gave no timetable for a ruling on the 10–12.5% levies. (BBG)  

US CCC-rated bond spreads crossed the 1,000bp distressed threshold for the first time since the 2023 banking crisis, reaching 1,007bp from 860bp at September’s start. Higher rates are intensifying refinancing pressure on the weakest borrowers. (BBG)  

Factory activity across Asia expanded in September thanks to the global AI boom, private surveys showed on Thursday, offering some relief to policymakers who are concerned about nagging cost pressures attributable to the US-Israeli war on Iran. (RTRS)

The BOJ’s September summary reinforced its shift toward preventing an inflation overshoot, with one member calling for faster hikes if prices deviate upward. It offered no clear signal of growing support for another increase in October. (BBG)  

Japan’s Tankan large-manufacturer sentiment rose to 24 from 22, its strongest since 2018 but below the 25 consensus. Large non-manufacturer sentiment fell to 35 from 37, while planned capex growth eased to 11.3% from 11.5%. (BBG)  

China’s Finance Minister Lan Foan signalled additional targeted fiscal support in an article on the ministry’s website. Proposals include broader interest subsidies, higher funding limits and potentially deploying unused local-government bond quotas to support consumption and investment. (BBG)  

South Korean September exports surged 83.5% Y/Y to a record $120.94bn, beating expectations of +65.4%; semiconductor exports more than tripled to $60.3bn. The trade surplus reached a record $49.85bn as AI demand continued to drive the expansion. (WSJ)  

Seoul pushed back on treating Alaska LNG as a done deal: President Lee said participation depends on commercial viability and legal compliance. Nuclear investments also require assessment plant by plant. (CNBC)

UK PM Burnham will launch his plan to recast Britain’s relations with the EU at a summit in November, after both parties put aside a dispute about Brussels’ “Made in Europe” initiative to ensure the delayed meeting takes place. (FT)

Copper’s cash price returned to a premium over three-month futures, signalling tighter prompt supply. Traders are weighing strike risks at an Antofagasta operation against Panama’s proposed mine restart, with China’s holiday reducing trading activity. (BBG)

US officials believe a Chinese invasion of Taiwan before 2028 is increasingly unlikely despite Chinese President Xi Jinping's instructions for his military to be ready by 2027 to take the democratically governed island by force, if needed, according to US sources. (RTRS)

Russia summoned Denmark’s ambassador over a September encounter between a Danish helicopter and a Russian warship, warning of escalation risks in the Baltic. Moscow and Copenhagen dispute whether the ship fired flares away from or toward the aircraft. (BBG)

Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos told Bloomberg’s Screentime conference the company is “not growing as fast as I want us to.” He said management is working to accelerate growth while acknowledging its own actions are creating headwinds. (BBG)

Google has unveiled Gemini 4 Argon, but access begins with a selected group of cyber defenders. Google says the model is designed for complex software engineering, enterprise knowledge work and cybersecurity, with testers providing feedback through its Fairwind program. Reuters reports no public release timeline, so developers and ordinary customers must wait for the promised wider access rather than treating this as an available public product.

Anthropic estimates current robots can perform tasks representing thirty-four percent of American work time under some circumstances. Its researchers say much of that capability depends on structured settings, while robots are currently cost-competitive for only 0.3 percent of job tasks. That gap matters for workers because technical exposure is an estimate of possible automation, not evidence that those jobs have already disappeared or will disappear next.

Google DeepMind wants AI-designed proteins to carry a detectable record of their origin. Its SynthID Bio research embeds watermarks in protein sequences and predicted structures, and the Nature paper reports near-perfect detection in its experiments with functional protein binders. Traceability could help identify generated biological designs, but Nature reports that redesigning proteins can obscure the watermark, and the signal itself is not a safety test.

Western Governors University reports that sixty percent of surveyed hiring professionals find real candidate skills harder to judge because of AI. Its survey included 3,128 American hiring professionals, with nearly one in five naming difficulty confirming whether an interview involved a human rather than AI as a top challenge. For job seekers, the finding highlights employers’ reported concern about demonstrating personal ability, although these survey responses do not establish actual hiring outcomes.

Indian AI tutoring company Arivihan raised ten million dollars to expand its learning platform. Prosus says the investment will fund research, local-language capabilities and geographic distribution, and reports that eighty percent of subscribers come from smaller cities and rural India. That planned expansion could widen tutoring access outside major cities, but investor-reported reach and student subscriptions do not prove better learning outcomes.

Vietnam’s September twenty-seventh funding notice offers businesses up to three billion dong for each AI application project. The National Technology Innovation Foundation sets the first application deadline for October tenth and plans to select fifteen projects before the end of twenty twenty-six. The grants could reduce the cost of testing local business solutions, but project selection and any resulting productivity benefits remain ahead.

Hitachi and FANUC are pairing artificial intelligence with industrial robots for factory validation. Their announced trials target parts picking and production changeovers at Hitachi factories, with customer deployment aimed for fiscal twenty twenty-seven. The companies want to address manual work and skills shortages, but those benefits are objectives of the trials rather than demonstrated customer outcomes.

Destro announced eight million dollars in seed funding on September twenty-ninth for its warehouse robotics software. The company says MothershipOS assigns tasks across robots while VisionOS handles on-robot perception and manipulation across hardware platforms. That approach aims to coordinate equipment from different makers in warehouse workflows, while the funding and company descriptions do not establish broad adoption or effects on jobs.

CoreSense’s September twenty-fourth results announcement described robots adapting to changing factory tasks and defects. The European consortium also reported inspection drones sharing awareness, a domestic robot making its reasoning visible and an open-source software toolbox. Those demonstrations could inform more flexible and understandable robots, but the consortium was still exploring commercial integration rather than reporting broad product deployment.

Britain’s AI minister is reportedly reviewing restrictions that can slow workers moving between technology employers. Sifted reports that Kanishka Narayan discussed non-compete clauses and lengthy notice periods after founders and investors called for limits on extended notice and garden leave. Any future reform could affect staff mobility and hiring, but the report describes a review comment without an adopted rule or stated timetable.

Munich startup Ahron raised 2.2 million euros to develop agents for human resources administration. https://t.co/n5WFawQKg4 reports that its planned automation includes employee onboarding, hiring-manager feedback and payroll audits across existing company systems. These are consequential employee processes, so the announced funding and product descriptions should not be confused with independently verified automation outcomes at scale.

Zenithon raised ten million dollars for AI models of extreme physics. Its backers describe work aimed at fields including fusion energy, rocketry and semiconductor manufacturing, with funding intended for model development and hiring. Faster physical modeling could support future energy and chip research, but the applications and investor speed claims do not establish commercial deployment or immediate consumer benefits.

Paris startup Blackfuel says it has more than 250 million dollars in contracted revenue for AI infrastructure. The company describes multi-year customer agreements and a first European computing cluster being developed with AMD and NTT DATA, with its first deployment scheduled for twenty twenty-six. The planned capacity could support organizations running AI services, but contracted revenue does not mean collected cash and the announcement does not establish an operating cluster.

ElevenLabs says a 300 million dollar employee share sale values the voice AI company at twenty-two billion dollars. The company reports that Wellington and T Rowe Price led the tender, and TechCrunch says employees could sell some vested equity. The concrete benefit is liquidity for participating employees, while the implied private valuation does not establish profitability or a public market price.

OpenAI and America’s Small Business Development Centers plan practical AI workshops for local businesses. OpenAI targets training about 150 advisers and reaching at least one thousand businesses in person, while the partner says workshop completers will receive free ChatGPT Plus access. Owners could gain instruction through existing advisory networks, but these figures are rollout goals and the announcement does not show training or business gains already achieved.

The Significance of the Cardiff MoU

Introduction

The Cardiff Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed on September 14, 2026, brings together political leaders from Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland around demands for greater self-determination and constitutional change. The development highlights tensions within the UK’s devolution settlement. 

Main Facts

Scotland: The SNP continues to advocate another independence referendum.

Northern Ireland: Sinn Féin supports eventual Irish reunification; the Good Friday Agreement provides a constitutional mechanism for a border poll under specified conditions.

Wales: The debate is primarily about greater devolution, although independence has gained more political attention.

The three positions therefore are not identical. 

The MoU also expresses support for closer European ties after Brexit.

Core Concept

Devolution → Regional Autonomy → Self-Government Aspirations → Constitutional Negotiation

The UK is a unitary state with extensive devolution, rather than a classical federation. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland possess different constitutional arrangements.

Why It Matters

The issue illustrates the tension between:

Territorial Integrity ↔ Self-Determination

It also raises questions about parliamentary sovereignty, regional identity, asymmetric devolution and constitutional flexibility.

Westminster’s Position

The UK Government has rejected immediate calls for independence referendums. A major legal reference point is the UK Supreme Court’s 2022 ruling that the Scottish Parliament cannot unilaterally legislate for an independence referendum without Westminster authorisation. 

Constructive Analysis

The MoU is politically significant but not itself a legal instrument capable of dissolving the UK. Its importance lies in collective political signalling and pressure for constitutional dialogue. Existing UK government guidance describes MoUs as non-legally binding arrangements. 

Way Forward

Strengthen intergovernmental dialogue

Clarify devolution powers

Establish transparent constitutional procedures

Respect democratic mandates while maintaining constitutional legality

Address regional economic and political grievances

Develop a sustainable multi-level governance framework

Highlighted Keywords

Devolution | Self-Determination | Parliamentary Sovereignty | Asymmetric Federalism | Territorial Integrity | Constitutional Reform | Regional Autonomy | Good Friday Agreement | Brexit | Multi-Level Governance

Conclusion

The Cardiff MoU demonstrates how regional identities and demands for autonomy can reshape constitutional politics without immediately producing state fragmentation. For India, it offers a comparative lens on managing diversity, regional aspirations and national unity through constitutional accommodation.

Apple origin :

    The apple of discord is a Greek mythology tale where Eris, the goddess of chaos, tossed a golden apple inscribed "To the fairest" into a royal wedding. It sparked a fierce quarrel among three goddesses Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite that led directly to the Trojan War.

The Wedding and the Golden Apple The Snub: 
     The sea goddess Thetis and her husband Peleus held a grand wedding. They did not invite Eris, the goddess of strife, because she only brought fights and bad moods.The Revenge: Mad about the slight, Eris crashed the party anyway. She threw a bright golden apple onto the banquet table.

More known religious concepts about the apple:

                 Lady of the Dead... Mictecacihuatl 

Goddess Mictecacihuatl, Santa Muerte

    Mictecacihuatl is the Aztec goddess of death and the "Lady of the Dead" who rules the lowest underworld, Mictlan, alongside her husband, Mictlantecuhtli.

    Dia de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) serves as the primary cultural bridge connecting   '' Goddess Mictecacihuatl, Santa Muerte ''

   The indigenous peoples of Mesoamerica ( Mexico through Belize, Guatemala, El Salvador, and parts of Honduras and Nicaragua, such as the Maya, Nahua (Aztec), Zapotec, Mixtec, and Olmec) practiced ancestral funerary cults long before the advent of Catholicism. These Mesoamerican rituals dedicated to the deceased date back over 3,000 years, significantly predating both Christianity and the institutional Catholic Church.
   However, a crucial historical nuance must be noted: indigenous populations did not originally observe these rituals on November 1st and 2nd. Rather, they operated within their own distinct chronological frameworks and seasonal calendars.

The historical timelines diverged as follows:
    • Mesoamerica (circa 1,000 BCE onward): The Olmec, Maya, and subsequently Aztec civilizations developed highly sophisticated funerary rituals. Within these cosmic worldviews, death was conceptualized not as a definitive end, but as a continuation of existence. This commemorative festival spanned an entire month, occurring during the ninth month of the Aztec solar calendar, which corresponds to modern-day August.
     • Europe (circa 1st–11th Century CE): Following the emergence of Christianity, the Catholic Church progressively formalized its liturgical calendar. Working in absolute isolation from the American continent, European ecclesiastical authorities designated November 1st and 2nd for the commemoration of saints and the deceased (All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day), deliberately absorbing and replacing indigenous European pagan traditions, such as Celtic festivals.

The Origin of Synchronicity

     The modern syncretism stems from the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire in 1521. Spanish conquistadors and chroniclers encountered a deeply entrenched indigenous veneration of the dead that far predated their own theological systems, yet occurred during the late summer.
    In an effort to facilitate religious conversion and eradicate indigenous pantheistic worship such as the veneration of the underworld goddess Mictecacihuatl, Spanish Catholic missionaries strategically transposed this ancient indigenous festival to align with the European liturgical dates of November 1st and 2nd.

In conclusion:

1.  Ritual Antiquity: The historical depth and spiritual framework of the cult belong definitively to the indigenous cultures of Mexico.
2.  Chronological Alignment: The specific calendar dates of November 1st and 2nd are derived from European Catholic tradition.
      Consequently, contemporary observations on these identical dates reflect two distinct cultural paradigms: the European tradition characterized by solemn, quiet remembrance at cemeteries, and the Mexican tradition, which manifests as a vibrant celebration featuring intricate altars and iconic skeletal iconography, a direct legacy of the Aztec ritual framework transposed onto the Gregorian calendar.

        '' Goddes Mictecacihuatl conversion in to Santa Muerte ''

    Many devotees and scholars view the Aztec goddess Mictecacihuatl as a historical and cultural predecessor or conceptual precursor to Santa Muerte, though they are not strictly the exact same "incarnated" entity.

Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) serves as the primary cultural bridge connecting Mictecacihuatl and Santa Muerte. It acts as a living timeline where ancient Aztec mythology, colonial Catholic forced integration, and modern folk spirituality converge.

The Connection

• Shared Roots: Mictecacihuatl was the ancient Aztec "Lady of the Dead" who ruled the underworld of Mictlan alongside her husband.
• Cultural Syncretism: When Spanish colonization suppressed indigenous religions, native beliefs went underground. Over centuries, pre-Columbian reverence for death figures merged with European Catholic iconography, eventually giving rise to the modern folk saint.
• Modern Interpretation: Many contemporary Mexicans and Mexican-Americans see Santa Muerte as a modern, syncretic manifestation or cultural continuation of Mictecacihuatl.

Key Differences

• Religious Context: Mictecacihuatl belonged to polytheistic Aztec mythology, whereas Santa Muerte is venerated within a folk-Catholic framework (despite being condemned by the official Catholic Church).
• Visual Depiction: While both appear skeletal, Santa Muerte is heavily influenced by the European Grim Reaper and La Parca, typically wearing flowing robes and holding a scythe or globe.

   The evolution from the Aztec goddess Mictecacihuatl to the modern folk saint Santa Muerte shows a fascinating cultural transition. While they share deep symbolic connections, the rituals and offerings for each reflect their distinct eras, one rooted in Mesoamerican cosmic balance and the other in contemporary folk Catholicism.

GOVERNOR MUTFWANG HIGHLIGHTS PLATEAU
AGRICULTURE, ENERGY AS POTENTIAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR EUROPEAN INVESTORS

Plateau State Governor, His Excellency , Caleb Manasseh Mutwang, Esq, has called for a new phase of partnership between Plateau State and the European Union, anchored on mutual benefit, investment and the exchange of greater opportunities.
The Governor made the call on Tuesday, September 29,2026 while hosting the Ambassador of the European Union to Nigeria, His Excellency Gautier Mignot, to a state dinner at the Banquet Hall of the New Government House, Little Rayfield, Jos.

Speaking on the backdrop of the Ambassador's engagements with key institutions in the State, Governor Mutfwang said Plateau was prepared to deepen its relationship with Europe while also positioning its agricultural, energy, educational and cultural assets for international partnerships.
The Governor identified agriculture as one of the sectors where Plateau could build a stronger international partnership, drawing attention to the State's diverse agricultural products and its capacity for expanded production.

"We believe that there are many things that we can offer
Europe as land for agriculture becomes more scarce in Europe. You can be sure that Africa is just beginning investments in agriculture," Governor Mutfwang said.

He said the emerging relationship should be driven by mutual respect and shared interests, rather than a one-sided expectation of assistance.

Governor Mutfwang introduced the EU Ambassador to acha, one of Plateau's indigenous cereals, after observing his appreciation of the meal. He also called for livestock and dairy production as another area with significant potential, noting that Nigeria continues to spend substantial resources importing dairy products despite the opportunities for local production.

Beyond agriculture, the Governor placed energy development high on the partnership agenda, expressing appreciation for the European Union's collaboration in exploring energy solutions for health institutions across the State. He specifically called for the actualisation of the 5-megawatt hydropower project at Assop Falls, supported through UNIDO, saying Plateau looked forward to seeing the project come on stream.

"We hope that we will see that come on stream as soon as possible," Mutfwang said.

He said Plateau had commenced preparations to develop the sector and expressed the State's desire to benefit from European experience and technology in moving towards modern livestock management.

"We hope that with your own experience we will leap from where we are into the mechanized stage of livestock management," he said.

Governor Mutfwang further urged the EU diplomatic community to look beyond Nigeria's major commercial centres and explore Plateau State, recalling earlier and potential European partnerships in agriculture and industry.

Responding, EU Ambassador His Excellency Gautier Mignot, expressed appreciation to Governor Mutfwang for the hospitality extended to him, describing his first visit to Plateau as an experience that had left a strong impression.

"I was very curious to see it firsthand when I heard a lot about the wonderful weather of Plateau State and beautiful landscapes. And I must say I haven't been disappointed at all," the Ambassador said.

He, however, singled out the hospitality of the people as one of the most striking aspects of his visit. "But the hospitality of the people of Plateau State, I think, is what impressed me most in the last three to four hours," he said.

The Ambassador also commended Governor Mutfwang's detailed knowledge of the partnership between Plateau State and the European Union, saying he was impressed by the Governor's understanding of the various areas of cooperation.

"I was very much impressed that His Excellency was fully knowledgeable about our partnership, much more than ours, by the way," Mignot remarked.
